name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana - Phase IV

whyItMatters: PMGSY has been the backbone of Sikkim's rural road network in steep, landslide-prone terrain, and PMGSY-IV targets 25,000 remaining unconnected habitations nationally with a relaxed population threshold for NE/Himalayan states. Sikkim's scattered hill hamlets (population norm lower for NE/hill states) are exactly the target category. The 90:10 Centre:State pattern for NE states makes it one of the cheapest ways for Sikkim to build all-weather rural connectivity, including climate-resilient designs now emphasised in the phase-IV framework.
eligibleApplicants: State Governments (Rural Development Departments) for eligible unconnected habitations
sikkimNodalDept: Rural Development Department, Government of Sikkim
whatCanBeFunded: New all-weather rural road connectivity to eligible unconnected habitations (62,500 km nationally under PMGSY-IV), including bridges/cross-drainage; upgradation under earlier verticals continues per existing sanctions.

fundingRatio: 90:10 Centre:State for the 8 North-Eastern states (including Sikkim) and Himalayan states; 60:40 for other states (confirmed in scheme material and parliamentary answers).

name: Regional Connectivity Scheme - Modified UDAN
agency: Airports Authority of India (RCS implementing agency)
period: FY2026-27 to FY2035-36 (10 years); Cabinet approved 2026, launched 4 July 2026.
whyItMatters: Modified UDAN replaces the expiring RCS-UDAN with a Rs 28,840 crore, 10-year programme - VGF of Rs 10,043 crore for airlines, Rs 12,159 crore for aerodrome development and Rs 3,661 crore for 200 helipads focused on hilly/NE/island/aspirational areas. For Sikkim this is the vehicle to keep Pakyong (a UDAN-operationalised greenfield airport with chronic viability and weather constraints) served, to add small-aircraft routes, and to bring its helicopter network (Gangtok-Bagdogra and intra-state heli services) under subsidised RCS heli routes. NE states carry only 10% of the VGF share versus 20% for other states.

sikkimNodalDept: Tourism & Civil Aviation Department, Government of Sikkim

fundingAvailable: National outlay Rs 28,840 crore over FY2026-27 to FY2035-36 (VGF Rs 10,043 crore; aerodrome development Rs 12,159 crore; helipad development Rs 3,661 crore).
